## Source 1 — TechCrunch: 2026年,AI将从炒作走向实用主义 (风闻 / guancha.cn translation, 2026)

**Type:** Industry analysis (TechCrunch Chinese translation)
**Headline:** "In 2026, AI will move from hype to pragmatism"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "如果2025年是AI接受'氛围检验'的一年,那么2026年将是这项技术变得实用的一年。行业焦点已经从构建越来越大的语言模型,转向更艰难的工作——如何让AI真正可用。"
> "在实践中,这涉及在合适场景部署更小的模型、将智能嵌入物理设备,以及设计能无缝集成到人类工作流程中的系统。"
> "2026年将是转折之年,行业将从暴力扩展转向研究新架构,从flashy(浮华的)演示转向有针对性的部署,从承诺自主性的代理转向真正增强人类工作方式的代理。"
> "规模定律不再奏效... 如今,许多研究人员认为AI行业正开始耗尽规模定律的极限,并将再次过渡到研究时代。"
> "Meta的[前首席AI科学家]Yann LeCun长期以来一直反对过度依赖扩展。"

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "规模定律不再奏效" — the named-anchor macro claim
- "暴力扩展 → 研究新架构" — the named-anchor shift
- "flashy演示 → 有针对性的部署" — the named-anchor shift
- Yann LeCun named-anchor as the "扩展怀疑论"权威

### Why this works:
TechCrunch is the canonical Western tech-press source. Their 2026 hype-to-pragmatism thesis is the **macro framing for the entire Pillar 6 cycle**. Pair with Source 2 (Manchester/Groningen academic study) for the "industry + academia both seeing the shift" two-source arc. **The "规模定律不再奏效" line is the strongest single macro claim.**

## Source 2 — Less hype, more drama: AI and the changing discourse of global news coverage (University of Manchester + University of Groningen, Digital Journalism journal, 2026)

**Type:** Academic study (Manchester + Groningen universities, Digital Journalism journal)
**Headline:** "Less hype, more drama: AI and the changing discourse of global news coverage"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "New research, co-authored by academics from the University of Manchester and the University of Groningen, adds nuance to the idea that journalists have hyped AI technologies."
> "Examining AI coverage in The New York Times (USA), De Volkskrant (The Netherlands), and Folha de S.Paulo (Brazil) between June 2020 and September 2023."
> "Although fascination with systems like ChatGPT was evident, the reporting often reflected deeper tensions and uncertainties about AI's future."
> "Instead of merely amplifying hype, the study highlights a recurring discourse of 'open-ended technological inevitability', according to which AI's impact is unavoidable, though its course remains uncertain."

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "Less hype, more drama" — the named-anchor academic framing
- 3 named newspapers (NYT / De Volkskrant / Folha de S.Paulo) across 3 continents
- "Open-ended technological inevitability" — the named-anchor academic term
- 3+ year study window (June 2020 → Sept 2023)

### Why this works:
This is the **academic counterweight** to the TechCrunch hype-to-pragmatism thesis. The Manchester/Groningen universities + Digital Journalism journal are the named-anchor academic sources. **The Scribe should hold both university names + the journal name exactly. This pairs with the 2026-06-24 brief's existing Idea 8 (Manchester/Groningen + TechCrunch) for continuity.**
